summary: Created a 6-phase plan adding WARN-only Check 8 (blast-radius-driven coarse file_scope declarations, default threshold 3) and Check 9 (exact + normalization-equivalent duplicates) to validate-state.sh, an opt-in --fix routed through the deployed mutex-guarded state-write.sh, a Create Task Mode Step 6.5 advisory in task.md, and regression fixtures asserting exit 0 despite warnings.

memory_candidates.content: In this repo's script layer, deploy-root posture is per-script and asymmetric, and that asymmetry constrains cross-script calls. state-write.sh (the single mutex-guarded specs/state.json writer) carries a deploy-root guard and hard-refuses to run from the agent-system/extensions/core source store; validate-state.sh is deliberately guard-free and argument-relative so it runs from both the source store and the deployed tree, and so it can validate out-of-tree fixtures. Consequence: any guard-free script that needs to WRITE state.json must resolve a state-write.sh copy whose own path lies under */.claude/scripts/ or */.opencode/scripts/ and refuse loudly (exit 2) when none exists -- it must never fall back to a hand-rolled 'jq > tmp && mv' write, which reopens both corruption channels (unguarded mutex, shared temp path) that state-write.sh exists to close. Verified empirically: the deployed copy writes an out-of-tree fixture correctly when given an absolute --state-file, so fixture-based tests still work through it.
